skills.name: identify_state_machine_dispatch
skills.definition: The reader recognizes that _draw and _update branch on a numeric mode variable to route between title, game, death, win, and help screens.
skills.evidence: _draw and _update functions dispatch on mode==0/3/6/9 to different draw/update pairs

skills.name: decode_level_array_indices
skills.definition: The reader interprets the unnamed positional fields of levels[hero.lvl][n] (e.g. [2]=treasure count, [5]=pirate count, [6][7]=map offset, [10]=fading platform count, [11][12]=spawn) by cross-referencing how each index is used.
skills.evidence: levels[hero.lvl][6],[7] used as map() offsets in gamedraw; [11][12] as respawn coords in fall()

skills.name: trace_map_coordinate_offset
skills.definition: The reader follows how world coordinates are converted to map-tile lookups by adding levels[hero.lvl][6]*8 and [7]*8 to hero.x/hero.y before fget/mget.
skills.evidence: tile_at calls in collision() add levels[hero.lvl][6]*8 and [7]*8 to x,y

skills.name: recognize_sprite_flag_encoding
skills.definition: The reader infers that fget/mget tile values in specific numeric ranges (60–69 doors, 34–44 treasure, 21–29 keys, ==2 ladder) encode object identity through flag arithmetic.
skills.evidence: collision() branches on behind>=34 and behind<=44, topleft>=60 and topleft<=69, tile_at==2

skills.name: infer_directional_facing_flag
skills.definition: The reader determines that hero.dr and pilocate[...][3] booleans encode left/right facing and are passed as the flip-x argument to spr().
skills.evidence: hero.dr set in btn(0)/btn(1) branches, used in spr(hero.sp,...,hero.dr); pilocate[...][3] toggled at edges

skills.name: parse_animation_cycle_pattern
skills.definition: The reader recognizes the move() helper increments hero.sp until it exceeds sprite+hero.ani then wraps, producing a sprite-cycling walk animation tied to movement.
skills.evidence: move(sprite) function and its mirror enemy_move(pisprite)

skills.name: detect_hardcoded_platform_heights
skills.definition: The reader spots that the platform check is a long disjunction of specific hero.y constants (8, 32, 56, …) instead of a tile-based query, and understands this constrains level geometry.
skills.evidence: platform = hero.y==8 or hero.y==32 or hero.y==56 ... in collision()

skills.name: trace_riding_platform_offset
skills.definition: The reader follows the hero.ron/hero.rx scheme where the player's position is computed as platform_x - rx so that holding left/right adjusts the offset rather than the absolute position.
skills.evidence: hero.x=travs[hero.lvl][1][1]-hero.rx in gamedraw; hero.rx+=1/-=1 in gameupdate movement branches

skills.name: decode_door_key_pairing
skills.definition: The reader works out that door sprite N and key sprite N share an index derived as topleft-59 / behind-20, and hero.keyheld must match dnum for deldoor() to fire.
skills.evidence: dnum=(topleft-59) and hero.keyheld==topleft-59 check in collision()

skills.name: infer_fading_platform_timing
skills.definition: The reader interprets the time() % fadewait modulo logic toggling tempon true/false based on the longest platform width on the current level.
skills.evidence: fadewait=2+(maxwidth-3) and time() % fadewait / time() % (fadewait*2) in gameupdate

skills.name: locate_exit_trigger_logic
skills.definition: The reader spots that an exit is recognized when behind==192 (sky tile flag) and the player's x/y falls within ±7 of an exits[] entry, with btnp(5) confirming the transition.
skills.evidence: if (behind==192) block in stats() iterating exits[hero.lvl]

skills.name: trace_cheat_flag_gating
skills.definition: The reader notes that cheat[2], cheat[3], cheat[5], cheat[6] gate enemy drawing, key placement, level-skipping, and ladder/travelator alternatives respectively.
skills.evidence: if cheat[2]==0 then ... enemy_update(); if cheat[5]==1 ... hero.lvl+=1; if cheat[6]==1 ... alt ladders

skills.name: identify_collision_corner_sampling
skills.definition: The reader recognizes that collision() probes specific corner offsets (top-left at x,y-1; top-right at x+w/2,y-8; floor_below at x,y+h) rather than the whole bounding box.
skills.evidence: topleft, topright, floor_below, ladder_d, ladder_u tile_at calls in collision()

skills.name: spot_pirate_gap_avoidance
skills.definition: The reader follows how pirates flip direction when their x aligns with templatforms gapleft/gapright edges on a matching y, simulating gap avoidance.
skills.evidence: for platloop loop inside enemy_update() comparing pix to gapright/gapleft

skills.name: match_init_update_draw_triad
skills.definition: The reader maps the PICO-8 lifecycle by locating _init calling titleinit(), and _update/_draw delegating to mode-specific update/draw pairs.
skills.evidence: _init at bottom calls titleinit(); _update and _draw branch by mode

skills.name: detect_dead_defunct_code
skills.definition: The reader notices comments like 'defunct' and 'fixme' marking the travelator/lift systems as legacy code that still runs but is shadowed by the fading-platform replacement.
skills.evidence: comments 'draw travelators if present - defunct' and 'move lifts - defunct' wrapping travs/lifts loops

skills.name: trace_respawn_coordinate_bug
skills.definition: The reader spots that fall() assigns hero.x=levels[hero.lvl][11] then immediately overwrites hero.x=levels[hero.lvl][12], so the y-respawn never lands in hero.y.

skills.name: recognize_centered_text_helper
skills.definition: The reader interprets centre_print(strtxt,py) as computing 64-(#strtxt*2) to horizontally center text on the 128-wide screen given 4-pixel glyph width.

chunk_summary: A complete PICO-8 platformer cart implementing a Manic Miner / Jet Set Willy style demake with mode-switched title/help/game/death/win screens, tile-flag-driven collision for ladders/doors/keys/treasure/exits, animated pirates with gap-avoidance, timed fading platforms, and a partly-abandoned travelator/lift subsystem.
